body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#115 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #176

## Summary

Two things: add four specific servers (Dropbox, Google Drive, Outlook, Tailscale), and give mcpx a channel for "you should add this" / "this one is slow, host it locally" so that the first thing is not a manual pipeline forever.

The second is the more interesting one, and the finding is that mcpx should **not** grow a curated vendor list. It already has registry search, live server add, and CLI→MCP adapters; what it is missing is the *memory and the ranking* — a record of what a user wanted and could not find, and enough metadata to answer "is there a better instance of this than the one I am using". A curated list of four servers is a snapshot that rots; a good search-add-record loop keeps working.

## Original notes

> - mcp-owned opencode api support
>   - add the dropboxMcp, googleDriveMcp, outlookMcp, tailscaleMcp
>   - please make an alias for the tailscaleMcp except it should not require auth it should accept the creds i already used to connect to it and the only skill it should provide is listTailnet and listHostnames
>   - accept user feedback, requests, routinely implement features/interfaces that are good idea. "you should add this mcp it's free." "this mcp is very good you should consider hosting it locally because the public one is slow and limited" 

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

| capability | where |
| --- | --- |
| search the public MCP registry | `GET /v1/registry/search`, `internal/registry/registry.go:153` (pins `version=latest` at `:158`; matches server names only, as a substring), `mcpx registry search\|show\|add` (`internal/cli/registry.go:15`) — there is no `mcpx connect` |
| add a registry server to config | `mcpx registry add <name>` prints the entry and the variables it needs; `--write` adds it (`internal/cli/registry.go:92-124`). No verify-it-starts step, no rollback. |
| add a server live, project or user scope | `POST /v1/servers` (`internal/api/ops_settings.go:82`) — `command`/`args`/`env` or `url`/`headers`/`transport`, plus `mcpx` extras |
| remove a server live | `DELETE /v1/servers/{name}` |
| expose one server as several filtered namespaces | `aliasOf` + `mcpx.tools` (`docs/story.md` §"Profiles and aliases") |
| wrap a CLI program as a server | `internal/adapter`, `paths.adapters` |
| wrap an OpenAPI service as a server | `internal/openapi`, `paths.apis`, `mcpx api --spec` |
| credentials | `mcpauth.Auth` on a server entry; `${VAR}` expansion in `APISpec.Headers`; OAuth for remote servers is **declared and not performed** (`docs/protocol.md` §6) |
| per-server latency and error statistics | `GET /v1/stats` — `calls`, `servers`, `instances`, `errors`, `sessions`, `volume`, `slowest` |
| a feedback channel | **none** |
| a record of a search that found nothing | **none** |

The statistics row matters: mcpx already measures exactly the thing the note's second quote is about ("the public one is slow and limited"). It measures it and does nothing with it.

## What exists for the four requested servers

Queried the official registry, `https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=<name>`, on 2026-09-30. Results are noisy — the same package is returned several times under different versions — and deduplicated here. (That is the raw API queried *without* `version=latest`. mcpx always sends the pin, `internal/registry/registry.go:158`, and gets distinct names — see #179.)

| requested | found | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Dropbox** | `io.github.pipeworx-io/dropbox` ("Dropbox MCP Pack — wraps the Dropbox API v2"), `ai.smithery/cindyloo-dropbox-mcp-server` (search/browse/read), `io.usefulapi/dropbox-sign` (a *different* product — Dropbox Sign) | no first-party Dropbox entry; all third-party |
| **Google Drive** | `search=google drive` → **0 results**; `search=gdrive` → **0 results**. Only `com.mcparmory/google-drive` surfaced, under `search=drive` | no first-party Google entry in the registry. The best-known Drive server is the `gdrive` **reference server** from `modelcontextprotocol/servers`, which was moved to the archived set. Effectively: nothing well-maintained and official. |
| **Outlook** | `io.github.chrischall/office-outlook-mcp` (mail, calendar, contacts, tasks), `io.github.0xka13b/microsoft-outlook-mcp` (read/search/send), `com.mintmcp/outlook-email`, `com.mintmcp/outlook-calendar` | no first-party Microsoft entry under this search. Microsoft ships MCP for other products; Outlook coverage here is third-party. |
| **Tailscale** | `io.github.YawLabs/tailscale-mcp` ("manage your tailnet from AI assistants"), `ai.dinglebear/rtailscale` (devices, routes, DNS, keys, users, ACLs — MCP **and** CLI), `ai.dinglebear/tailscale-rmcp` (Rust MCP server and CLI) | no first-party Tailscale entry. |

Two conclusions:

1. **None of the four has a first-party server.** Every option is community-maintained, of unknown quality, and requires handing it a credential to a fairly consequential account. That is a reason to prefer the thinnest possible wrapper, not the richest one.
2. **Three of the four have an excellent official CLI or HTTP API, which mcpx can already consume without any MCP server.** `tailscale` the CLI covers `status --json` (hostnames, tailnet, devices) and the Tailscale API is documented and simple; Microsoft Graph and the Dropbox API v2 both publish OpenAPI-ish documents. So `internal/adapter` and `internal/openapi` are a **better** route than adopting a third-party server: the declaration is reviewable, the credential handling is `${VAR}` expansion, and there is no extra process from an unknown author in the trust path.

**For the specific tailscale request** — an alias exposing only `listTailnet` and `listHostnames` — the cheapest correct answer is an **adapter spec over the `tailscale` CLI**, about fifteen lines:

```jsonc
{ "name": "tailscale", "command": "tailscale",
  "tools": [
    { "name": "listTailnet",   "args": ["status", "--json"], "json": true },
    { "name": "listHostnames", "args": ["status", "--json"], "json": true }
  ] }
```

It requires no auth because the local `tailscale` CLI is already authenticated — which is the literal reading of "it should accept the creds i already used to connect to it". The renaming and narrowing that an *alias over a real MCP server* would need is the `toolViews` work in #114; the adapter route needs none of it, because an adapter declares its own tool names. Worth doing as the first proof that adapters are the right default for this class of request.

## Approaches

### Approach A — least recommended: ship a curated list of vendor servers in mcpx's defaults

Bundle known-good entries for Dropbox, Drive, Outlook, Tailscale and others in `internal/defaults`, so `mcpx registry add dropbox` just works.

Why not:

- **It is a snapshot of a directory that already exists and is maintained by someone else.** The registry is the curation layer; duplicating a slice of it into a Go binary means every entry rots at its own rate and a stale one is worse than no entry, because it carries mcpx's implicit endorsement.
- **It makes mcpx an opinion about third-party code quality** across products it does not use, for a trust decision (handing over a Dropbox or Microsoft 365 credential) that is genuinely consequential and genuinely the user's.
- **It answers the wrong question.** A user asking for "the Dropbox MCP" wants Dropbox capability, not a specific package. The registry answers "which packages exist"; nothing today answers "which of these should I use", and a hard-coded list does not answer it either — it just hides the question.
- It also scales badly: there are thousands of servers and four is not a stopping point anyone will respect.

### Approach B — middle: make discovery and adoption good, and document the four as recipes

Improve what exists rather than adding a list:

1. **Registry metadata in search output.** The registry carries more than name and description; surface what it has — package type, transport, remote-or-local, version recency, whether it is official. "Is this maintained" is the first question and today the answer requires leaving mcpx. Part of it is already fetched and thrown away: each result's `_meta` is decoded into `listResponse` (`internal/registry/registry.go:137-146`) and dropped at `:168-169`. It carries `io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official` with `status`, `publishedAt`, `updatedAt` and `isLatest` (checked live 2026-09-30).
2. ~~**Deduplicate registry results.** The raw responses above return the same server up to nine times across versions. `internal/registry` should collapse by name and show the newest version, which is a small, clearly-correct fix (visible directly in the query output quoted above).~~ **Struck (issues pass, 2026-09-30, at 05c78b2):** mcpx never sees those duplicates. `Search` pins `version=latest` on every query (`internal/registry/registry.go:158`), every caller goes through it, and five live searches returned all-distinct names (#179). The duplicates belong to the un-pinned raw query above, which mcpx does not issue. What #179 found instead, and owns: `registry.pageSize` is only consulted when `limit <= 0` (`:155`), and `nextCursor` is parsed (`:143`) and dropped, so a search silently stops at one page.
3. **`mcpx registry add <name>` end to end** (this issue first called it `mcpx connect`, which does not exist; the command is `mcpx registry`): search, pick, show what it will run and what credentials it wants — `registry show`/`add` already do this much — add it at project or user scope, verify it starts and lists tools, and roll back if it does not. `POST /v1/servers` plus `/v1/health` already provide the rest.
4. **Prefer an adapter or an OpenAPI declaration when one is available.** When a requested capability has a well-known CLI or published API document, say so: *"`tailscale` is installed; an adapter declaration needs no credential and no third-party process. Generate one?"* That is a better default than adopting an unknown server, and it connects directly to the spec-generation work in #114.
5. **Ship the four as documented example declarations**, in `docs/`, not in defaults — copy-pasteable, reviewable, and obviously not endorsed-and-maintained by mcpx.

This is all deterministic and most of it is small.

### Approach C — recommended: B, plus a recorded feedback loop that mcpx can actually act on

Do B. Then close the loop the second bullet is asking for — and note that the useful version of it is mostly **evidence mcpx already has**, not free text.

**1. Record the misses.** Every `mcpx search` and `registry search` that returned nothing or was followed by no call is a data point. Store them (the event store, #6, is the natural home) and expose `mcpx feedback` / `GET /v1/feedback` as the local list: *"you searched for calendar 6 times in 3 sessions and never called a tool."* That is a concrete, unarguable statement of a missing capability, derived at zero cost from telemetry that already flows through `/v1/log`.

**2. Turn statistics into a recommendation.** "This mcp is very good you should consider hosting it locally because the public one is slow and limited" is a *measurement*, and `/v1/stats` already has `slowest`, `errors` and `volume` per server. A `mcpx doctor` check — and `doctor` already exists (`internal/cli/doctor.go`) as the place mcpx tells you what is wrong — can say: *"`notion` (remote): p95 4.2s over 340 calls, 6% errors. A local package exists in the registry. Switch?"* Remote-versus-local is visible in the config (`url` versus `command`), and the registry says whether a local package is published. This is the single best item in this issue: it is deterministic, it uses only data mcpx already collects, and it produces exactly the advice the note quotes.

**3. Accept explicit feedback as a first-class record.** `mcpx feedback "add a calendar mcp"` / `POST /v1/feedback`, appended to a local file with the context mcpx can attach automatically (which servers are configured, which searches failed, what the daemon version is). Local by default and never transmitted anywhere. Its purposes, in order: it gives the user a place to put the thought, it gives `mcpx prompt` something to act on, and it gives a maintainer a file to paste into an issue if the user chooses to.

**4. Let the prompt layer read it.** With #113's `intent --scope ops`, *"add the thing I keep failing to find"* becomes: read the miss log, search the registry, propose a server or an adapter declaration, show the plan, add on confirmation. Every step is an existing declared operation; the model only chooses among them. That is "routinely implement features/interfaces that are good idea" in the only form that is safe — mcpx proposing, the user approving.

**5. Explicitly out of scope: mcpx modifying itself in response to feedback.** The note's "routinely implement features" could be read as self-modification. It should not be. The loop ends at a proposal a human accepts; anything past that is the arbitrary-provisioning question deferred in #113.

Recommended because it converts a vague "accept feedback" into three concrete, mostly-deterministic features built on data mcpx already has; because the slow-remote-server recommendation is genuinely valuable and genuinely cheap; and because it avoids taking on the maintenance and the implied endorsement of a vendor list.

## Open questions

- Where do feedback and miss records live — the event store (#6), a plain JSONL file in the state dir, or the log store? The log store has query, filtering and retention already; a separate file is simpler to hand to a maintainer.
- Should a miss record capture the *query text*? It is the useful part and it is also the most sensitive thing in the file. Local-only mitigates it; an explicit opt-out setting is probably still required.
- Does `mcpx registry add` verifying a server by starting it constitute running untrusted code before the user consented? Almost certainly — the consent has to come before the first launch, not after.
- Is there a registry field for "official/verified"? The `io.github.*` versus `com.*`/`ai.*` namespacing implies provenance but does not assert maintenance. Partly answered: per entry, `/v0/servers` returns `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/official"]` with a lifecycle `status` (e.g. `active`) and dates — registry lifecycle, not a quality or verification signal.
- Should mcpx ever propose *self-hosting* a remote server automatically (pull the package, run it locally, rewrite the config, keep the credential)? Attractive and a large step; the rollback story if the local one is worse must exist first.
- For Google Drive specifically: with no maintained server, is a Google Drive **OpenAPI declaration** (Drive API v3 publishes a discovery document) the better answer? Probably, and it generalises to every Google API at once.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (S for richer metadata + the four example declarations — registry dedup struck, see #179; M for `mcpx registry add` end-to-end and the doctor recommendation; M for the feedback/miss store) · **Impact** medium-high — the doctor recommendation and the miss log are the parts that keep paying; the four servers are a day's config each once adapters are the route.

**Depends on / related**: #179 (registry search gaps: unreachable `registry.pageSize`, dropped `nextCursor`; disproved the dedup premise), #6 (event store, for miss records), #76 (ops/CLI parity for any new operation), #5 (config chain, for add scope). Siblings: #114 (`toolViews.from` is what an alias over a *real* tailscale MCP server would need; adapter/OpenAPI generation is the recommended route for all four), #109 (a miss is a search that found nothing — the two share the record), #113 (`intent --scope ops` is what acts on the feedback), #110.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.
